rows.statement: The overflow plate, linkage and drop cylinder operate the tub stopper through the overflow opening; the tee and trap connections sit in the concealed drainage assembly.
rows.status: Manufacturer instructions reviewed; existing model unknown
rows.limit: Do not assume the stuck assembly is a Watco 500/501/600TL.

rows.statement: Watco steps 6–7 describe removing the overflow plate and drop-cylinder assembly and readjusting it; a SLIP LOCK is inserted through the overflow with the lever down/open.
rows.limit: Not proof this fused/stuck unit can be extracted safely from above.

rows.statement: Ask the provider to identify the model and attempt the least-destructive tub-side adjustment/removal before cutting finished surfaces.
rows.status: Proposed control based on owner preference
rows.limit: Provider must judge safety; do not force a stuck linkage.

rows.statement: Heise’s Ingleside case says it accessed the exterior ceiling to remove the old overflow and replace the tub waste-and-overflow assembly.
rows.limit: “Exterior ceiling” is not confirmed to mean the storage-unit ceiling below this tub. No drywall-restoration proof; self-published; embedded 404 block persists.

rows.statement: Heise's Plumbing publishes four SF tub waste-and-overflow/gasket cases (Ingleside #163802, Mission #158154, Marina #176011 and Panhandle #171358), including downstairs ceiling access to locate pipes and test fittings, and advertises plumbing-access drywall/ceiling patching.
rows.limit: Neither proves this exact stuck-lever extraction or ceiling restoration.

rows.statement: Opening a ceiling below the tub requires restoring drywall/plaster, taping, texture and paint, plus confirming under SFBC §106A.2(10) whether the ceiling between unit and storage/garage below is part of a fire-resistive assembly (e.g., Type X gypsum).
rows.limit: Building age and whether the ceiling separation is fire-resistive are unknown; lead/asbestos screening and fire-rated assembly confirmation apply before cutting.

rows.statement: Watco step 7 readjusts the drop cylinder to ensure the drain stops water when closed; DBI requires inspection before pipes are covered.
rows.limit: Model-specific instruction; actual test/inspection sequence depends on confirmed assembly and permit.

rows.statement: Consider a serviceable access solution, but the operative access-panel dimension was not verified from a free official code source.
